issues.t: Turbocharger failure
issues.sym: Loss of power, a whistling or grinding noise from the engine, blue or white exhaust smoke, or coolant that keeps disappearing.
issues.why: The small turbo is cooled by both oil and coolant. Its seals and the coolant and oil lines feeding it can leak, and some turbos fail outright, sometimes leaking coolant into the turbo.
issues.next: Have it checked quickly if power drops or coolant goes missing. Ask the shop to test the wastegate and check the coolant and oil lines before replacing the whole turbo.

issues.t: Low power and turbo underboost
issues.sym: The engine feels flat or sluggish, especially when merging or climbing, often with a check engine light and code P0299.
issues.why: The turbo is not making full boost. Common causes are a sticking or worn wastegate, a cracked turbo outlet hose, or leaks in the intake and PCV system.
issues.next: Have the codes read and a smoke test done for boost leaks. Small parts like a hose often fix it; do not let a shop jump straight to a new turbo without testing.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the water pump, housings and turbo lines
issues.sym: The low coolant warning comes on, a sweet smell after driving, drips under the front of the car, or weak heat at idle.
issues.why: The 1.4L turbo has several plastic coolant housings and small turbo coolant lines that crack or let their seals go, and the water pump can start to seep.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with Dex-Cool and have the leak found with a pressure test. Fix it early so the engine does not overheat.

issues.t: PCV valve cover failure and whistling
issues.sym: A high-pitched whistle or squeal with the engine running, a rough idle, lean codes, hesitation, or oil being burned.
issues.why: The PCV valve is built into the plastic valve cover. Its diaphragm tears, which causes a vacuum leak and pulls oil into the intake.
issues.next: Have the valve cover checked for a vacuum leak. The usual fix is a new valve cover with a built-in PCV valve.

issues.t: Power loss in very cold weather
issues.sym: In below-freezing weather the engine loses power or goes into reduced power mode, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: Moisture in the intake and PCV system can freeze in the charge air cooler or hoses. GM issued a bulletin for this icing problem.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for the cold-weather bulletin (19-NA-227) and any software or parts updates.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the oil pan and engine seals
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or oil needing to be topped up between changes.
issues.why: Owners report leaks at the oil pan, the oil cooler area and other seals on the 1.4L turbo.
issues.next: Have the leak traced before it gets worse. On all-wheel-drive models the oil pan job takes longer because other parts must come off first.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine quits while driving or when slowing to a stop, sometimes with warning lights.
issues.why: Owners report stalling and engines that stopped working. Causes vary and include sensor, fuel and turbo problems.
issues.next: If it stalls, get safely off the road. Have the stored codes read right away, since steering and brakes get heavier when the engine is off.

issues.t: Check engine light that keeps coming back
issues.sym: The check engine light returns after emissions repairs, often with evaporative system codes.
issues.why: Leaking EVAP purge or vent valves and other emissions parts can set repeat codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the EVAP system smoke-tested. Make sure the gas cap clicks tight.

issues.t: Dead battery
issues.sym: The car won't start or cranks slowly, sometimes with several warning lights, even at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report batteries going dead early. A weak battery or loose battery cable can also cause odd warning messages.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and the cable ends checked for tightness.

issues.t: Clogged catalytic converter
issues.sym: Loss of power, a check engine light, or a rotten egg smell.
issues.why: A converter can clog, often after the engine has been burning oil or misfiring.
issues.next: Fix any oil burning or misfire first, then replace the converter so the new one is not ruined.

issues.t: Bubbling paint
issues.sym: Paint bubbles or peels, often around trim and edges.
issues.why: Owners of 2013 Encores report paint bubbling at about 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer if any goodwill help is available, and get rust treated early.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: Owners report leaks or failed A/C parts on the 2019 model.
issues.next: Have the A/C system leak tested before recharging it.

issues.t: Front airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; an airbag light may come on.
issues.why: A diagnostic test in the airbag module software could switch off the front airbags and seat belt pretensioners.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 16V-651 and 17V-437. The dealer reflashes the software free.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets heavy, with a power steering message.
issues.why: The steering column housing could wear through the power steering circuit board.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-146. The dealer replaces the steering column as needed, free.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak from stop/start part (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid leaking, or the car losing drive.
issues.why: Bolts may be missing from the end cap of the stop/start accumulator on the transmission.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-668. The dealer replaces the accumulator free if bolts are missing.

issues.t: Front seat may come loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat may shift on its tracks.
issues.why: An incomplete weld on a seat bracket can let the seat break loose in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-446. The dealer inspects and replaces the seat track if needed, free.

issues.t: Lap belt pretensioner may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The front lap belt pretensioner cables may not stay locked after firing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-488. The dealer replaces both front pretensioners free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not inflate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: A bad weld on the passenger front airbag inflator on some 2013 Encores could stop it from deploying.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-298. The dealer replaces the passenger airbag free.

issues.t: Key can be removed out of Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out of the ignition when the shifter is not in Park, so the car could roll away.
issues.why: A part in the ignition key cylinder lock housing can wear.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 16V-502; the dealer fixes it free.

issues.t: Block heater cord can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Cracked insulation on the engine block heater cord; there may be a burning smell if it shorts.
issues.why: On some all-wheel-drive Encores, the block heater cord can crack in very cold weather and expose wires.
issues.next: Stop using the block heater and check your VIN for recall 14V-417. The dealer replaces the cord free.

issues.t: Heated steering wheel bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Play or clunking in the steering wheel.
issues.why: On a small number of early cars with a heated steering wheel, the wheel bolt may not have been fitted properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-105 and have it repaired free.

issues.t: Airbag module left in factory mode (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on.
issues.why: On a handful of vehicles the airbag module was never switched out of factory mode, so the airbags would not deploy.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-774. The dealer reprograms the module free.

issues.t: Front seat bolts may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat rocks or moves at the back.
issues.why: The rear bolts holding one or both front seats may not have been installed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-537. The dealer installs the bolts free.
